notes: Preserves current P3 verse selections; suggestions must not silently add biblical text.
Witness edition collation and oral read-through remain open for every movement.
Gospel accounts and Catholic/Challoner/Crampon verse numbering must not be silently harmonised.
Editorial context is not represented as Scripture in the theatre.

movements.title: The Forerunner and first disciples
reviewFindings: Matthew 3:1–6 to 3:11–17 omits 3:7–10; test Johannine preparation and baptism handoff without invented summary.
Matthew 4:1–11 remains context-only. Verify narrative transition to Mark 1:14–15 and John 1:35–51; do not turn omissions into a synthetic chronology.

movements.title: The Kingdom in Christ's teaching and signs
reviewFindings: M21 title promises teaching and signs, but Mark 2:1–12 is currently editorial context, not selected biblical reading. Test truthfulness of title and necessity of one narrated sign.
Retain full Beatitudes and Lord's Prayer according to the present locks; check whether Matthew 6:9–15 begins sufficiently for readers.

movements.title: Christ the Bread of Life
reviewFindings: John 6:1–15 (loaves) is context-only, while the Bread of Life discourse begins at John 6:26. Review whether the sign must be Scripture or an explicitly labelled editorial lead-in.
Check John 6:35 to 6:47 gap for omitted objection and agency; no automatic insertion.

movements.title: Peter's confession and the Transfiguration
reviewFindings: Matthew 16:13–28 precedes 17:1–9; assess the six-day transition and the omission of 17:10–13.
Keep Peter's confession, Passion prediction and Transfiguration distinct in visual staging.

movements.title: The approach to Jerusalem
reviewFindings: John 11:1–44 has multiple selected discontinuous ranges; read every seam for agency and causal continuity.
John 11:45–53 plot against Christ remains HS-CF-05 candidate; determine whether the Passover approach needs this Scripture bridge.

movements.title: The King's entry into Jerusalem
reviewFindings: Matthew 21:1–11 supplies the royal entry. Test segue to Last Supper without assuming an exact chronology or inventing Holy Week dialogue.

movements.title: The Last Supper and Christ's final teaching
reviewFindings: Luke 22:7–20 selected for Eucharistic institution. John 14:16–17 is HS-CF-09 proposed bridge, not an approved interleaved Gospel speech.
Keep New Covenant theological relation distinct from historical-place certainty and separate evangelist voice.

movements.title: Gethsemane, betrayal and trial
reviewFindings: Matthew 26:36–75 and 27:1–2,11–26 jump between interrogation phases. Check omitted setup, interrogators and Pilate scene agency.
John 19:1–16 is editorial-context-only, not automatically stitched into Matthew; preserve distinct Gospel accounts.

movements.title: The sacrifice on Calvary
reviewFindings: John 19:17–30 ends with death; John 19:38–42 burial remains HS-CF-06, to test before reading the empty tomb.
Crucifixion must remain Scripture-led and not be presented as a geocoded exact event site simply because traditional sites have coordinates.

movements.title: The risen Lord and his witnesses
reviewFindings: John 20:1–3,6–9,11–18 has gaps at 20:4–5 and 20:10; check who sees and who returns.
Luke 24:13–35 Emmaus remains context-only, not part of selected continuous reading; check whether Resurrection witness coverage remains sufficient.

movements.title: The Ascension and promised mission
reviewFindings: Acts 1:3–5 is HS-CF-07 bridge; check that Acts 1:6–12 does not open mid-conversation without adequate context.
Map the Ascension site, if at all, as traditional/regionally qualified rather than certain.

movements.title: Pentecost and the first Church
reviewFindings: Acts 2 selection omits several intervening verses; verify Pentecost, Peter's speech and response remain coherent.
Acts 7:51–53 HS-CF-08 precedes Stephen's martyrdom at 7:54–59; compare Challoner versus Crampon Acts 7:59–60 numbering before wording claims.

movements.title: Saul and the Gospel to the Gentiles
reviewFindings: Acts 9:1–11 and 9:17–22 omit Ananias narrative details; ensure who acts and Saul's baptism are not left unintelligible.
Acts 10 is highly discontinuous; verify Cornelius's summons, Peter's vision, meeting and Holy Ghost descending with no false geography or harmonization.

movements.title: Antioch, apostolic missions and the Council
reviewFindings: Acts 11, 13 and 15 form large time jumps; ensure Council of Jerusalem is not presented as directly following initial Antioch commission without any intervening mission.
Keep apostolic journeys optional/canonical Atlas destinations, not a speculative exact route through every modern point.

movements.title: The Gospel proclaimed in Rome
reviewFindings: Acts 19:21 and 28:16 are HS-CF-10 and HS-CF-11; test whether Rome intention and arrival are indispensable to Acts 28:23–31.
Rome city context may be mapped using canonical Atlas authority, without adding an invented archaeological path.

movements.title: Christ and the Lamb in heavenly vision
reviewFindings: Revelation 4 heavenly throne is editorial context-only; Revelation 5 Lamb is selected. Check whether the vision begins with adequate scriptural setting.
Apocalyptic vision must switch away from the terrestrial geographical map.

movements.title: The final conflict and judgment
reviewFindings: Revelation 12 is editorial context-only and Revelation 19–20 selected; check whether the final conflict and judgment are intelligible without falsifying visionary sequence.
Treat figures, times and places as apocalyptic vision, not dateable events on a modern route.

movements.title: The New Creation
reviewFindings: Revelation 21:1–7 and 22:1–5 are selected, but the broader canonical book continues; ensure theatre ending does not falsely assert these are the last verses.
Preserve the New Creation's visionary genre, including no terrestrial coordinates.
